brief: Oil is range-bound long-term, with the 200-day average flat, but speculative positioning has turned aggressively bullish while physical buffers stay thin, leaving the market crowded against supply relief yet convex to further disruption. GS's Quinn reports managed money added a cumulative $9.3bn of Brent longs from August 4 to September 8, 70% short covering and 30% new longs, pushing net length to the 88th percentile of its two-year range as November Brent rose 25.7%. From September 8 to 15 Brent surged another 11.1% on Houthi advances toward Bab al-Mandeb and Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline closure, adding $8.3bn in open interest, then partly reversed, Brent down 2.7% and open interest down $1.3bn, after reports Saudi could restore about half the pipeline's capacity within days. Oil volatility has stayed calm despite the rally, not confirming a spot panic, favoring call spreads over chasing spot. JPM's commodities team says it has no baseline view for the endgame since the Iran conflict began. A move to $85-90 needs the pipeline fixed, no escalation and weaker demand. A move to $110-120 needs only one more disruption, because with buffers this thin, missing barrels, not sentiment, are driving price.
